summary: Built in 1920 by L. T. Kinsley; a steel tower replaced the blown-down wooden one; the Green Mountain Club restored it in 1984, when the cabin was demolished.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, built 1938-40 to replace a wooden one
facts.status_note: Standing, but the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists its cab as no longer in place.

access.note: Reached on foot by public hiking trails, the Long Trail and the Forester's Trail.

visit.trail_note: Park at the Eden Crossing lot on VT-118, follow the Long Trail about 2.2 miles to the Forester's Trail junction, then 0.2 miles to the summit.

events.note: Tower built by L. T. Kinsley; he had built a cabin the year before
Lightning struck the tower and splintered it
Old wooden tower blown down in the September hurricane (reported January 1939)
Steel tower built 1938-40; the 1939 newspaper planned WPA funding, the state report credits the New England Forest Emergency fund
A 1956 guidebook calls the tower recently abandoned; a summit watchman was employed that June
Fire warden began the season at the tower
Replacement trailer-style cabin airlifted onto the summit by helicopter
Green Mountain Club restored the tower in the summer
Summit cabin demolished during the 1984 restoration

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The January 1939 newspaper expected WPA money to pay for the replacement; the state report for 1938-40 credits the New England Forest Emergency fund. We could not settle which account is right.
A 1956 guidebook calls the tower recently abandoned, but a summit watchman was employed that June and a fire warden served there in 1961.
The 1920 newspaper and the Green Mountain Club give L. T. Kinsley; a 1924 newspaper gives E. L. Kinsley. The initials differ, but this is probably the same watchman.

sources.title: Belvidere Mountain (newspaper and state report extracts)

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 21.0 (from OpenStreetMap) does not match the 45 ft 9 in height the January 1939 paper gave for the planned replacement. Left out of facts and corrections for a human to settle. FFLA marks the cab as gone, but the GMC 1984 account does not mention a cab, so that is unresolved. Summit land owner and climbing safety were not checked; access is set to public only from trail guides. Newspaper quotes come from the Eastern U.S. Lookouts transcriptions, not the originals. The Kinsley initials differ between sources.
